cards.question: Should a tool returned in the evening be bookable the next morning?

blocks.paragraph: The spec has seven morning pickups and seven evening returns, but it never says whether a tool returned tonight can be booked again tomorrow morning. This one is yours to call, because it depends on whether lenders want a night to check a tool or want it back out on loan straight away.

bullets: If a returned tool can go straight back out, each tool is borrowed more often and fewer tools are needed.
If it cannot, every tool gets a rest day, so lenders can check it but borrowers wait longer.
Either way the spec needs one clear sentence about it before the build starts.

context.title: The line that leaves it open

blocks.quote: Each day has one pickup slot and one return slot, and every booking covers one tool for one borrower.

options.label: Let a returned tool be booked the next morning
options.consequence: Each tool is borrowed more often and fewer tools are needed, but a tool may go out before the lender has checked it.

options.label: Require a rest day between bookings
options.consequence: Every tool is checked between loans, so tools stay in good shape but borrowers wait longer and more tools are needed.

recommendation.text: Let a returned tool be booked the next morning.
recommendation.reason: Most neighbours lend tools to save others a purchase, and a quick turnaround is the common way to do that.

cards.question: Is the loan-length rounding rule what you meant?

blocks.paragraph: When the app counts the days of a loan, it rounds a part day up to the next whole day. The rule decides whether a borrower is held to too many days or too few, and that is a product choice.

blocks.quote: Loan lengths on a booking are rounded up to the nearest whole day.

recommendation.reason: Rounding up avoids an argument about a late return, and the spec already says the exact hours are shown before rounding.

cards.question: Do you want past bookings kept after the tool is returned?

blocks.paragraph: The spec covers making and editing a current booking. It says nothing about what happens to that booking once the tool is back.

bullets: Keeping old bookings means more storage.
It also means a new screen to browse them.
That makes it a call about scope, so it is yours.

cards.question: Which day should a booking window start on?

blocks.paragraph: A booking window covers seven days in a row, but the spec does not name the first day. That day decides where one window ends and the next begins, and lenders disagree about it.

blocks.quote: A booking window covers seven consecutive days.

options.label: Start the week on Monday
options.consequence: Windows line up with the working week, but a lender who hands tools over on a Sunday is booked across two windows.

options.label: Start the week on Sunday
options.consequence: A Sunday handover covers the week ahead, but windows no longer line up with the working week.

recommendation.reason: Most calendars and work schedules begin on Monday, so windows match how people already think about the week.

cards.question: Should a booking remember a borrower's safety training?

blocks.paragraph: Today a person can borrow any tool on the shelf. The spec says nothing about skills or safety training. Remembering them would add a settings screen and a filter on every tool list, so this is a scope call.
